page.overview:
Who is Citipes?

(not to be confused with Citipati) is a genus of caenagnathid that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta, Canada. Only one species has been assigned to this dinosaur: Citipes elegans.

Like Caenagnathus, it has a convoluted taxonomic history; it has been previously assigned to the genera Ornithomimus, Macrophalangia (a synonym of Chirostenotes), Elmisaurus, Chirostenotes, and before being given its own genus in 2020. The identification of several autapomorphies allow Citipes to be distinguished from its contemporaries and its closely related genera.

The specimens belonging to Citipes comes from the Dinosaur Park formation, a geological dig site renowned for famous dinosaurs like Styracosaurus and Parasaurolophus.

Citipes is indirectly mentioned in the description of Elmisaurus in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute. The website refers to a species of Elmisaurus from North America that some scientists believe that it is actually Chirostenotes. This is referring to Elmisaurus elegans, who has been recognised as the new genus Citipes in 2020.
